newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George too busy for near-term bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George too busy for near-term bid.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said it remained on the lookout for acquisitions such as Bank of Melbourne Ltd but its near-term focus would be on absorbing Advance Bank after their A$2.6 billion merger.

St George chief financial officer Steve McKerihan said chairman Frank Conroy had confirmed the bank's continuing acquisition strategy at a meeting with shareholders of the merged group in Melbourne on Monday.
"I think what the chairman was saying in terms of our strategy (is that) if an opportunity did arise such as the Bank of Melbourne that would be consistent with our strategy," McKerihan told Reuters.
"But that is not to say that anything would happen in the near future."

McKerihan said while St George could afford to acquire Bank of Melbourne, which had a market capitalisation of about A$1.07 billion, the current focus of the Sydney-based regional bank was on operational rather than financial issues.

"So if such an opportunity did emerge the timing would be very inopportune. It is really the operational issues that we are confronting on integration (with Advance). That is more the issue rather than our financial capacity."

Westpac Banking Corp, one of Austsralia's big four, has often been cited by analysts as a likely bidder for Bank of Melbourne which, like St George, is regarded as a second-tier regional bank specialising in home loans rather than big ticket corporate activities.
Bank of Melbourne shares were 17 cents higher at A$8.25 at 1.50 p.m. (0250 GMT).
